The risk analysis addresses uncertainty under Texas law about enforcing limitation-of-liability and/or indemnity provisions drafted to New York precedent.
The memo states that the Playbook-approved institution and rules are AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules with Large Complex Case Procedures.
The memo states that the Level 2 fallback is JAMS Comprehensive Arbitration Rules.
The memo states that Castlebridge demands ICDR International Arbitration Rules.
The risk analysis discusses ICDR’s materially different discovery limitations, specifically Tribunal-directed document exchange under Article 22.
The risk analysis addresses ICDR expedited-procedure thresholds that may automatically apply to counterclaims under $500,000.
The risk analysis addresses differences in ICDR’s default confidentiality scope compared with AAA/JAMS.
The memo states that the Playbook-approved mediation period is 60 days.
The memo states that the Level 2 fallback mediation period is 45 days.
The memo states that Castlebridge demands a 30-day mediation period and that either party may file an arbitration demand if no mediator is appointed within 15 days.
The memo quantifies estimated settlement-savings loss as $2,860,000, derived from $13,000,000 ACV × 22% average mediation-settlement discount.
The memo lists the Playbook-approved consequential-damages waiver carve-outs as (a) willful misconduct, (b) breach of confidentiality, and (c) IP infringement indemnity.
The memo states that the Level 2 fallback adds (d) data-breach notification costs.
The memo identifies Castlebridge’s additional carve-out (e) as delay damages, liquidated or unliquidated.
The memo identifies Castlebridge’s additional carve-out (f) as third-party bodily-injury claims arising from Meridian’s services.
The memo quantifies maximum delay-damages exposure at $25,200,000, calculated as $4,200,000/month × 6-month overrun.
The memo flags a coverage-gap risk under Meridian’s $10,000,000 professional-liability policy for bodily-injury claims that could exceed the aggregate limit.
The memo states the Playbook-approved position as an absolute waiver of class, collective, and consolidated arbitrations, with no joinder without mutual written consent.
The memo states that the Level 2 fallback permits joinder of project-specific subcontractors with all-party consent.

The memo states that Castlebridge demands the right to consolidate any related arbitration involving its subcontractors or affiliates without Meridian’s consent, with the Tribunal having discretion to order consolidation.
The memo references 14 active subcontractors on the Gulf Corridor program.
The memo quantifies incremental defense cost exposure as $1,050,000–$1,650,000, derived from a $750,000 solo baseline versus $1,800,000–$2,400,000 for consolidated multi-party proceedings.

The memo states total quantifiable tail-risk exposure of approximately $29,710,000, or a reasonable rounding such as $29.7M, combining mediation-discount loss (~$2,860,000), delay damages ($25,200,000), midpoint incremental defense costs (~$1,350,000), and ~$300,000 of additional incremental or indirect items.
The memo applies a 12% dispute-probability factor for infrastructure engagements ≥ $5M ACV.
The memo states probability-weighted expected loss of approximately $3,565,200, or a reasonable rounding such as ~$3.57M, calculated as ~$29,710,000 × 12%.
